title: Tool-list defaults constrain the real turn entry points
pins: Requested names can narrow a mode, never widen it by default. Record actual model offers and native refusals, alongside independently prewritten authority expectations. A consumer moving a read-only session between languages must not accidentally offer a registered destructive tool merely because caller input names it.
scope: Normal published PHP send/stream and TS/Py send/structured entry points. Port-only explicit legacy opt-out, configuration migration and malformed flags remain additional native unit controls. No stream capability is invented in either port.
findings: PHP legacy sessions silently intersect foreign names, whereas ports preserve a typed tool_not_available refusal. All forms keep the mode ceiling. Named sessions refuse foreign names. Default empty lists offer no tools. Raw native outcomes retain these differences.
